summary: Pin tiebreaker logic causes unexpected fallback to lower-tier model during proportional canary
description: Issue summary: During a proportional canary rollout for rwd-v2.1 -> rwd-v2.0-quantized, several NimbusChat sessions that had an explicit model pin unexpectedly routed to the lower-tier quantized variant. Impact: customer-visible quality regressions for 12% of pinned sessions over a 2 hour window (reduced answer fidelity & hallucination rate increase). Environment: prod us-east, dedicated tenant for NimbusChat. Observed behavior: routing layer applied the canary proportion correctly overall but a tiebreaker path in the node-level pin resolver favored instance affinity over the explicit tenant pin when a specific set of backend nodes were under transient load. Expected behavior: any explicit tenant pin should always win; fallbacks to canary or lower-tier model only when pin target is unavailable or unhealthy. Timeline: 2026-03-10 09:55 UTC - customer reported quality drop; 2026-03-10 10:05 UTC - Support acknowledged and opened ticket; 2026-03-10 10:30 UTC - SRE ran targeted routing trace; 2026-03-10 11:15 UTC - mitigation applied to adjust tiebreaker priority; 2026-03-12 - follow-up analysis in progress.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer pins tenant route to model rwd-v2.1 using route config with explicit tenant_pin=true
2) Start a proportional canary that routes 20% of new traffic to rwd-v2.0-quantized in us-east
3) Simulate transient node CPU pressure on a subset of serving nodes (e.g., throttle background jobs to raise latency)
4) Observe routing traces for pinned sessions: some resolve to rwd-v2.0-quantized instead of rwd-v2.1 when the node-affinity tiebreaker selects a different host
5) Check per-request metadata for routing decision_reason and pin_source fields in traces

investigation_notes: Observed 112 affected requests in a 2 hour window; 12% of pinned sessions routed away from explicit pin.
Dashboard links: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/routing/tenant-pin-ops?org=nimbuschat (live metrics show spike correlating with high queue depth on svc-a-07)

Trace sample: req=8f3b shows decision tree: pinned_target check -> available_hosts filter -> host_health_rank -> tiebreaker (node affinity) -> selected host lacked pinned model binary warm cache -> fallback to quantized variant on same host
Hypothesis 1: comparator order allowed node affinity to outrank explicit tenant pin in edge conditions (race between health calc and pin resolution).
Hypothesis 2: warm cache mismatch: pinned model binary not yet loaded on preferred host leading runtime to report unhealthy briefly and trigger fallback path.
Repro in staging: synthetic queueing reproduced path when host_health temporarily flagged as degraded; unit tests currently missing for pin precedence.
Related configs: routing.tiebreaker.order (current: [host_health, node_affinity, tenant_pin]); should be [tenant_pin, host_health, node_affinity]—proposed change.
Risk assessment: low risk to overall platform but high customer impact for pinned tenants; change gated to region-scoped rollout & feature-flagged PR.
Work items: add audit log field 'pin_enforced' to all routing decisions, add unit tests for ordering edge cases, update canary coordinator to honor explicit pins when computing proportions.
resolution: Mitigation: Updated runtime config to prioritize tenant_pin over node_affinity in us-east (hotfix rolled at 2026-03-10 11:05 UTC). Customer reports improvement. Next steps: merge PR that hardcodes comparator order + adds audit logs (PR #1423), rolling canary for change scheduled 2026-03-15 to minimize blast radius. Follow-up: add automated test in canary-coordinator and include pin precedence checks in rollout playbook.
resolution_notes: Hotfix applied to make pin precedence absolute in region us-east; monitoring shows affected rate dropped to 0.3% of pinned requests.
PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/1423 created and under review to make comparator change permanent with tests.
Ops runbook updated: 'If tenant pin regressions observed, apply regional tiebreaker override and notify Platform Eng.'
